When AI writes code, who guarantees it works? Leo de Moura—creator of the Lean theorem prover and AWS Distinguished Scientist—says formal verification is the answer. In a recent Data Exchange podcast, he showed how Lean’s blend of functional programming and interactive theorem proving lets us turn informal intent into precise, machine‑checked contracts.

AI now assists in two critical steps: extracting pre‑ and post‑conditions from comments to generate specifications, and automating proof steps that would otherwise be tedious. This “auto‑formalization” reduces the manual proof burden that kept formal methods niche.

A concrete success story is Rust verification. By encoding Rust’s semantics in Lean, developers can automatically generate proof obligations for AI‑generated functions, proving functional correctness, absence of undefined behavior, and security policy compliance.

The vision is a verified software stack where every layer—from kernels to applications—carries formal contracts, and AI agents operate within sandboxed, provably safe policies. This shift creates new roles—specification and verification engineers—bridging domain expertise with rigorous engineering.

Read more about this emerging landscape and its implications for engineers and researchers. https://buildwithsaksham.in/blog/ai-lean-and-the-future-of-formal-verification
